The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```java
containsLib1Jar = (containsLib1Jar || line.endsWith(lib1JarStr) || lib1JarPatYarn.matcher(line).matches());
containsLib2Jar = (containsLib2Jar || line.endsWith(lib2JarStr) || lib2JarPatYarn.matcher(line).matches());
```
Reason:
The use of `endsWith` for checking the presence of JAR files was too strict, leading to false negatives when the actual output contained the required JAR files but did not match the exact end of the string. This caused the test to fail even when the JAR files were present.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
containsLib1Jar = (containsLib1Jar || line.contains(lib1JarStr) || lib1JarPatYarn.matcher(line).matches());
containsLib2Jar = (containsLib2Jar || line.contains(lib2JarStr) || lib2JarPatYarn.matcher(line).matches());
```
Reason:
The change from `endsWith` to `contains` allows for a more flexible check for the presence of JAR files in the output, ensuring that the test correctly identifies the required JAR files regardless of their position in the string. This resolves the issue of false negatives and ensures the test passes when the JAR files are indeed present.
